actions.justification: Mandatory first step. Patient has HR 118, BP 195/110 - tachycardia and severe hypertension require immediate documentation and continuous monitoring per AHA guidelines.

Mandatory - AHA Class I recommendation to obtain and interpret ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact to evaluate ST changes and confirm NSTEMI vs STEMI pattern. Already showing ST depression V1-V4.
Mandatory - Immediate history and physical for risk stratification. Cocaine-associated chest pain has specific considerations including vasospasm vs true ACS; history will guide management decisions.
MANDATORY: Activate cath lab immediately to meet door-to-balloon time <90 minutes. Patient is 15 minutes into presentation; time is critical.
MANDATORY: Aspirin 325mg chewable is first-line antiplatelet therapy for ACS/STEMI. Must be given immediately as dual antiplatelet therapy is Class I recommendation.
MANDATORY: P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor preferred) as part of dual antiplatelet therapy per ACS guidelines. Class I recommendation for STEMI/high-risk NSTEMI.
MANDATORY action: Heparin or enoxaparin anticoagulation is required as part of NSTEMI/STEMI management to prevent further thrombus formation. This is the highest priority remaining mandatory action.
Primary PCI must be arranged urgently to meet the door-to-balloon <90 minute target. Cath lab has been activated; arranging PCI is the next critical step.
IV access is essential to administer anticoagulation, medications, and any resuscitative drugs. Required before or concurrent with drug administration.

Cardiology consultation is critical for this cocaine-associated NSTEMI/STEMI with severe hypertension (195/110) and tachycardia. Specialist guidance needed for medication selection (e.g., beta-blocker use in cocaine setting), ongoing management, and PCI planning.

High-sensitivity troponin at presentation is a Class I recommendation for NSTEMI workup. Baseline troponin establishes the degree of myocardial injury and serial values will confirm diagnosis and trend.

Formal ECG interpretation of the ST depression in V1-V4 is needed to confirm NSTEMI pattern, assess for posterior STEMI equivalent, and guide further management including whether right-sided leads are needed.

Patient has significant hypertension (195/110) and tachycardia (HR 118) in the setting of cocaine-associated NSTEMI/STEMI. Beta-blockers are indicated to control heart rate and reduce myocardial oxygen demand. Note: cocaine is a relative consideration, but current guidelines support beta-blocker use when hemodynamically indicated in cocaine-associated ACS, especially with severe hypertension and tachycardia.

Patient has severe hypertension (MAP 138) and ongoing chest pain. Nitrates can reduce preload, myocardial oxygen demand, and help manage hypertension. There is no inferior STEMI pattern noted (ST depression V1-V4 suggests anterior ischemia), so RV infarction is not the primary concern here. Nitrates are appropriate to manage symptoms and BP.
Obtaining prior ECG for comparison helps differentiate new versus old ST changes and confirm the dynamic nature of ECG findings, supporting risk stratification and guiding interventional urgency.
Patient has SpO2 of 97% which is borderline; supplemental oxygen should be considered given active ischemia and tachycardia. Monitoring and readiness to administer if SpO2 drops is indicated.

While this appears to be anterior NSTEMI/STEMI with ST depression V1-V4, a right-sided ECG should be obtained to rule out RV infarction, which would contraindicate nitrates (already given) and guide fluid management. Important safety check before additional interventions.

Patient has ongoing chest pain with significant hypertension (195/110) and tachycardia (HR 118). In cocaine-associated ACS, pain management is important; however morphine should be used cautiously. If pain persists despite other measures, morphine may be considered.

At 90 minutes since arrival, door-to-balloon target of <90 minutes is at risk of being exceeded. Consider fibrinolysis as a backup if PCI cannot be performed within guideline timeframe, especially given this high-risk NSTEMI/STEMI presentation with elevated troponin and significant ST changes.

Patient has elevated HR of 118 and elevated BP, but given cocaine-induced vasospasm and NSTEMI context, cautious IV fluid support may be appropriate to maintain hemodynamic stability while awaiting PCI. This is the only available action not yet completed.

Patient has elevated HR of 118 and elevated BP; while most mandatory actions are complete, crystalloid support may be considered for hemodynamic monitoring. This is the only remaining available action not yet completed. However, given the hypertensive state (BP 195/110), this should be used cautiously and only if clinical assessment supports volume administration.

Calculate GRACE or TIMI risk score for this high-risk NSTEMI patient (elevated troponin 0.8, ST depression V1-V4, tachycardia, hypertension) to formally document risk stratification per AHA Class I guidelines for NSTEMI management.

Formally assess eligibility for early invasive strategy (within 24 hours). This patient has multiple high-risk features: elevated troponin, dynamic ST changes, tachycardia, and severe hypertension — meeting AHA Class I criteria for early invasive approach.

Admit to CCU given high-risk NSTEMI with cocaine-induced vasospasm/thrombosis, severely elevated BP (195/110), tachycardia (HR 118), and elevated troponin requiring continuous cardiac monitoring and intensive management.
